record.title: Kasumbalesa trucker obstruction and broader crossing closure in autumn 2022
record.scope: Kasumbalesa crossing, changing from northbound freight disruption to broader trader obstruction
record.direction: Varied by phase; both directions operating again in 6 October field accounts.
record.movement: Northbound heavy vehicles initially; Congolese small traders and wider crossing movements during escalation.
record.exceptions: Southbound traffic reportedly continued during the initial truck refusal; later scope broadened.
record.imposing_authority: Protesting truck drivers; Zambian police also closed the crossing during 5 October disturbances
record.enforcement: Driver obstruction and stone throwing, followed by police intervention and gate closure.
record.consequences: Freight queues and interrupted cross-border commerce.
record.record_type: Mixed non-state blockade and state closure
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present closure is inferred.
record.official_rationale: Drivers sought safety guarantees on DRC routes; police intervention followed disorder. Reported killings were disputed by official inquiries.
record.context: A late September strike preceded a clearly documented wider gate closure on 5 October. These phases are kept together to avoid double counting.
record.uncertainty: First coercive onset is unknown: closure was reported by 3 October, while broader interruption is documented on 5 October. One archive dates resumption to 5 October; stronger operational accounts confirm passage on 6 October. Stable complete normalization is unproved.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. The reported 24 hours concerns the broad 5–6 October phase, not the whole trucker episode; no exact interval assigned. Actual reopening labels observed passage within the recorded scope; the date is confirmation by that day, not a proven first resumption or durable end.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Freight News reports northbound driver blockage; Actualite reports wider obstruction; Okapi observes restoration.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. Drivers demanded safer working routes and officials responded to disorder. Contested reports of killings are not endorsed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Driver security demands explicit; mayor contests homicide allegation, which remains attributed.
Changing freight and trader categories at Kasumbalesa; no entire Zambia–DRC shutdown.
Differing phases and onset exclude exact interval despite one-day description of broader phase.
